rows.note: Use 睇法 as the all-purpose Cantonese noun for someone's opinion, assessment, or perspective.

example.english: I want to hear your take on this matter.
example.traditional: 我想聽吓你對呢件事嘅睇法。
example.jyutping: ngo5 soeng2 teng1 haa5 nei5 deoi3 ni1 gin6 si6 ge3 tai2 faat3

rows.note: Use 攞 as the all-purpose colloquial verb for physically getting, removing, or carrying something.

example.english: Please take a chair over here for me.
example.jyutping: bong1 ngo5 lo2 zoeng1 dang3 gwo3 lai4

rows.note: Use 揀 when take means choose or pick rather than physically take something.

example.jyutping: nei5 zi6 gei2 gaan2 fan2 lai5 mat6 laa1

rows.note: Use 食藥 specifically when take means ingest medicine.

example.english: Remember to take your medicine, and do not slack off.
example.jyutping: gei3 zyu6 sik6 joek6 m4 hou2 tau1 laan5

rows.note: Use 鏡頭 specifically for a film recording made continuously without a break.

example.english: This take has to be filmed in one go; we can't stop.
example.traditional: 呢個鏡頭要一次過拍，唔可以停。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 geng3 tau4 jiu3 jat1 ci3 gwo3 paak3 m4 ho2 ji5 ting4
